newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-Gold Fields Q1 pre-capex profit down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gold Fields Q1 pre-capex profit down.

text.p: Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd on Thursday got the first quarter gold reporting season off to a poor start when it posted sharply lower pre-capex net profit mainly due to a lower gold price received.

Gold Fields -- the world's third largest gold producer -- said its pre-capex net profit for the three months to end-March dropped 29 percent to 236.42 million rand from 333.08 million in the previous quarter.
It blamed the drop on the bullion price and the effect of the Christmas holiday period which led to a drop in production.
Although the group's three gold mines lifted output by 2.4 percent to 23,448 kg from 22,902 kg, the lower average gold price received offset the increase in output.
Gold Fields received an average 51,737 rand a kg of gold in the March quarter, a drop of around eight percent on the average 56,292 rand/kg in the three months to end-December 1996.

But Gold Fields' executive director for gold operations, Allan Munro, told a results presentation the group expected the present increase in gold output to be maintained while the average gold price received in the second quarter would be around the same as in the March quarter.

"With the jacking up of operations, we do anticipate and increase in gold production to be extended in the next quarter...the gold price (received) will average at least what we achieved in the past quarter," Munro said.

The group's gold mines milled or treated 2,829,000 tonnes of ore in the three months to end-March, down on the 2,885,000 in the previous quarter. Capital expenditure in the quarter under review was 205.88 million rand against the 235.29 million in the quarter to end-December.
The average yield increased to 8.3 g/t from 7.0 in the previous quarter while working costs increased to 41,593 rand/kg from 41,132 in the three months to end-December.
The worst performer of the mines was Kloof Gold Mining Company Ltd which posted pre-capex net profit of 54.63 million rand -- against 114.52 million in the previous quarter.
"If you ask what keeps me awake at night. It is Kloof," Munro said.

He said underground production at the Kloof division of the mine was adversely affected by an underground fire while problems with pumps and the No 3 shaft man winder also contributed to the drop in profits.
But Munro said Kloof and the Leeudoorn and Libanon units of the company were expected to produce more gold next quarter.
Driefontein Consolidated Ltd and Deelkraal Gold Mining Company Ltd would also increase gold production slightly in the next quarter.
Driefontein, which produced 12,139 kg of gold in the March qurter from the 11,232 kg in the December quarter, posted a 182.02 million rand pre-capex net profit down from 214.09.
Deelkraal reported a 230,000 rand loss from a pre-capex net profit of 4.47 million in the quarter to end-December.
Gold Fields was helped by good performances from its base metal and coal operations.
The best performer, unlisted Zinc Corporation of South Africa Ltd lifted its pre-capex net profit to 25.22 million rand from 9.95 million in the three months to end-December.
But Gold Fields' Northam Platinum Ltd continued its losses, reporting a net loss before capex of 18.44 million rand from the 1.78 million rand loss in the previous quarter.
Northam Director Peter Janisch said the poor perforamnce was due to a lower platinum price and also the effect of Christmas holidays when eight days of production was lost.
He said Northam remained a marginal operation but there was hope. "We are not drowning yet," he said.
He added that the company might approach banks for loans.
"If you see light at the end of the tunnel, you might go into debt to tide you over".
-- Johannesburg newsroom, +27-11 482 1003
